overview: Systematic review of routine caregiver burden screening followed by referral or support in memory clinics and similar specialist dementia services.
population: Studies of family caregivers of people with dementia in specialist services.
exposure: Routine burden screening followed by referral or support; studies of support alone and of tool accuracy are classified separately and reported as indirect evidence.
procedures: The library searches four databases and two grey literature sources in November 2026. Two reviewers screen and extract independently. Each study is classified as screening plus referral, support for identified caregivers, or tool accuracy. Risk of bias is assessed with design-appropriate tools. English and Spanish reports are included.

outcomes.name: Caregiver burden
outcomes.measure: Change in a validated burden scale, as standardised mean difference

outcomes.name: Care home admission of the person with dementia
Referral uptake
outcomes.measure: Proportion of referred caregivers attending support

feasibility: About 50 hours per reviewer covers an expected 1,200 records and 20 to 30 included studies.
biasMitigation: Studies classified by comparison before synthesis

parsimony.simplestPath: Three study classes, one primary outcome, equity and uptake extracted.

theoreticalFramework: None; the classification by comparison organises the review.
summary: Review protocol that separates screening from support.
